family: epoch-2 production (smollm3, sixth and final model)
single_variable_under_test: num_train_epochs 1 -> 2; every other protocol v2 variable held

1_frozen_data_hashes.status: PASS (same disclosed orders.csv exception, re-proven inert AT SMOLLM3'S RENDER LAYER)
1_frozen_data_hashes.evidence: 5 of 6 pinned files match protocol_v2.json exactly; orders.csv carries the known dated drift. Rendering all 15,203 rows through SmolLM3's template (with enable_thinking=false, as training uses) against both orders.csv versions gives the identical fingerprint 5f7baa9662794cad1c622666e57503eb9c8755bb3775a026246b72926ad03534 with an identical order_id sequence. SIXTH distinct per-model fingerprint (granite cb762cc6, phi 38fc4698, qwen 5f14347c, gemma 208431c8, ministral c4a95beb). Six different values from the same 15,203 records is the concrete justification for re-deriving this per model.
1_frozen_data_hashes.action_taken: none. orders.csv untouched, protocol hash not re-pinned.

2_adapter_targets_match_validated_set.evidence: q/k/v/o/gate/up/down -> 30,228,480 trainable of 3,105,327,104 (0.97%), identical to epoch-1 smollm3-v2. The largest trainable fraction of the six.

3_template_alignment_train_vs_gguf.evidence: reports/epoch-2/production/gates/smollm3_template_alignment.json: 7/7 including gguf_template_equals_hf_template TRUE (string-identical). Markers occur once each; the closed <think></think> block is present in the training render.
3_template_alignment_train_vs_gguf.reasoning_kwarg_check_requested: SmolLM3's template DOES branch on enable_thinking (thinking_capable_template: true). No warning fired because --template-kwargs was supplied, which is the correct behaviour. Across all six models the detector now reads: qwen TRUE, gemma TRUE, smollm3 TRUE, granite FALSE, phi FALSE, ministral FALSE -- it discriminates rather than warning indiscriminately.

4_native_fit_no_sysmem_spill.status: PASS expected -- but SmolLM3 sat exactly AT the ceiling in epoch-1
4_native_fit_no_sysmem_spill.evidence: epoch-1 smollm3-v2 measured 9.0 GiB allocated / 23.9 GiB reserved against a 23.889 GiB ceiling -- effectively AT the limit, arguably a hair over. A real measurement at the identical configuration.
4_native_fit_no_sysmem_spill.why_not_probe_based: the 12-step probe reports 9.0/13.1 GiB. All five prior probes underpredicted (epoch-1's own smollm3 smoke said 15.3 vs 23.9 actual), so it confirms only the trainable count and step time.
4_native_fit_no_sysmem_spill.spill_avoidance_applied: PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True (see below). No prediction is made; the full training log is the authoritative record.

spill_avoidance_investigation.goal: avoid touching the marginal PCIe link at all, without changing what the model learns

option_A_tested_and_ADOPTED.what_it_does: allocator-level only: lets CUDA caching-allocator segments grow in place instead of allocating fresh fixed-size blocks, which is what fragmentation accumulates in. It changes NO arithmetic and NO batch composition.
option_A_tested_and_ADOPTED.evidence_it_is_free: a 10-step probe produced BIT-IDENTICAL losses to the untuned 8x2 baseline (0.261, 0.2724, 0.2258, 0.2187, 0.2135, 0.213, 0.1915, 0.217, 0.185, 0.1853 in both). Not 'close' -- identical.
option_A_tested_and_ADOPTED.why_it_targets_the_right_thing: the observed epoch-2 drift is fragmentation-driven: allocated memory was stable in all five prior models (granite 9.3->9.3, phi 11.2->11.2, qwen 10.8->10.8, gemma 12.5->12.5) while RESERVED drifted (phi +2.1, gemma +2.3). expandable_segments attacks exactly that mechanism.
option_A_tested_and_ADOPTED.limitation: a 10-step probe cannot demonstrate a fragmentation benefit, since fragmentation accumulates over thousands of steps. Both probes read 13.1 GiB. This is a best-effort measure that cannot hurt, not a guarantee.

option_B_tested_and_DECLINED.change: per-device batch 8 -> 4 with grad_accum 2 -> 4, preserving effective batch 16
option_B_tested_and_DECLINED.explicitly_permitted: the frozen protocol sanctions this: training_frozen.batch.rule = 'native-fit rule from v1: reduce per-device only if reserved memory exceeds physical, keep effective 16, disclose'. It is pre-registered, not a deviation.
option_B_tested_and_DECLINED.it_works: probe reserved fell 13.1 -> 9.2 GiB, a 3.9 GiB reduction, and losses matched to 3-4 significant figures with the first two steps bit-identical -- floating-point accumulation-order noise, not a different objective.
option_B_tested_and_DECLINED.why_declined_anyway: adopting it would make SmolLM3 the ONLY model in the six-model epoch-2 family trained at a different microbatch split, and its epoch-1 counterpart used 8x2. Over 1,902 steps the FP-noise divergence compounds, so the final adapter would differ from an 8x2 run much as a different seed would. That is a second difference in a comparison whose entire purpose is to isolate ONE variable, introduced in the final model where cross-model consistency matters most for the synthesis. Option A achieves the same defensive goal at literally zero cost, so there was no need to spend comparison purity on it.
option_B_tested_and_DECLINED.recommendation: validated and available. Use it for any FUTURE run where avoiding spill matters more than matching this family's microbatch config.

checkpointing_decision.rationale: observed crash-to-crash intervals during training are 11, 14, 37 and 73 minutes. At ~4.6 s/step, 100 steps is ~7.7 minutes -- inside the SHORTEST observed interval. The default 250 (~19 min) is what cost 11 minutes and produced no usable checkpoint at ministral's step-128 crash. Cost is ~19 checkpoints; save_steps provably does not alter training math.
checkpointing_decision.override_test_note: if this run crashes, the resume will pass --save-steps 100 while the checkpoint also records 100, so the SaveIntervalEnforcer override path would AGAIN be a no-op. A genuine override test requires CLI and restored state to disagree, which has not occurred in any crash so far.

watch_item_specific_to_smollm3: SmolLM3 epoch-1 already sits at 12/0/0 on robustness -- the floor, like ministral. Ministral showed that 'already at the floor' does NOT mean nothing happens: its robustness barely moved (12/0/0 -> 12/1/0) while edge-holdout clean-10 fell 80% -> 60%, the largest edge drop of the five. Damage that cannot show on a saturated axis surfaces elsewhere. Watch for the same displacement rather than assuming a flat non-result.
decision: LAUNCH smollm3 epoch-2 at 8x2 with expandable_segments and save_steps 100
